title: Degradation Ladder and Safety-Net Routing for Canary / A/B / Shadow Deployments
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When we roll out model variants across regions and capacity tiers we currently rely on static fallbacks (simple region failover or model switch). This has led to partial outages and noisy rollbacks when traffic patterns or semantic differences between variants weren’t detected early. This ticket proposes a structured 'Degradation Ladder' and a safety-net routing runtime to govern canary rollouts, A/B tests, and shadow traffic.

Goals:
- Define a multi-step degradation ladder that maps SLA tiers -> capacity tiers -> model fidelity (quantization/variant) -> region fallback.
- Implement compatibility scoring for model variants (semantic and API-level) so fallbacks only occur to compatible variants or trigger safe-quarantine.
- Add synthetic shadowing and live replay probes to detect quality regressions under canary traffic before promoting or failing.
- Implement auto-rollback with hysteresis and a cooldown window to avoid flip-flopping.
- Provide observability: per-gate metrics, impact attribution (latency/cost/quality), and an incident-safe rollback action for Console and API.

Proposed Design Summary:
1) Degradation Ladder (runtime policy):
   - Step 0: Primary variant in customer region / dedicated capacity.
   - Step 1: Reduce throughput by admission control (latency-first tier) while keeping primary variant.
   - Step 2: Switch traffic to compatible lower-cost variant (same family, validated via compatibility score).
   - Step 3: Route to cross-region dedicated nodes if local capacity constrained.
   - Step 4: Fall back to host-shared pool with prefix-KV-caching and reduced max tokens.
   - Step 5: Safe degrade to a quantized small model with explicit customer notification.

2) Variant Compatibility Scoring:
   - Compare output distributions on synthetic prompt set (embed similarity + token-level diffs).
   - API compatibility checks (schema, function-calling surface).
   - Score used as a precondition for automatic variant switch during degrade. Thresholds configurable per-customer.

3) Canary / Shadow Probes:
   - Shadow traffic is replayed to candidate variants with synthetic probes that include both production-like and adversarial prompts.
   - Probes produce a drift score and latency/cost delta. Canary gate closes if drift > X or latency regresses > Y.

4) Auto-Rollback with Hysteresis:
   - Use rolling windows (5m/30m/3h) and three-state gate: Healthy / Degraded / Quarantined.
   - On Quarantined, a rollback plan will execute: (a) immediate traffic shift to last-known-good variant; (b) schedule deeper analysis; (c) notify on-call and customer-facing channels.
   - Cooldown: require stable healthy metrics for 30m before allowing reattempt.

5) Routing Engine Changes:
   - Policy evaluation layer that compiles a degradation ladder into a deterministic routing DAG.
   - Fast path for per-request routing decisions with cached policy decisions for tenant-region pairs.
   - Integrate cost-tier signals (billing and token-rate) and real-time capacity signals from scheduler.

Success Criteria:
- Canary gate prevents promotion when quality drift (semantic similarity) exceeds thresholds in >95% of trials.
- Mean time to safe rollback <= 3 minutes for severity-high regressions during canary ABs.
- No user-facing error rate increase during cross-region failovers in controlled experiments.
- Admins can visualize the current degradation ladder state in Console (per-deployment).

Backward-compatibility / Safety Considerations:
- Default ladder is conservative; customers can opt into more aggressive degradations.
- Manual overrides allowed in Console; audit logs for every auto-rollback decision.
- Security review required for policy execution surface that affects cross-tenant routing.

Implementation Phases:
- Phase 1 (Spike): compatibility scoring prototype, simulated ladder in dev. (Spike done)
- Phase 2 (Runtime): implement policy compiler & fast-path routing, synthetic probe harness. (In Progress)
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created by Asha Kapoor after incident post-multiregion deploy where canary promotion caused 15% semantic drift for a high-volume customer.

2026-02-24: Architecture spike complete. Prototype compatibility scorer (embedding + token-diff) implemented in spine-service: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/spine/pull/712. Results: synthetic set detected drift in 4/5 failing deployments in replay tests.

2026-02-28: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Decisions: (1) implement policy compiler in routing-service, (2) expose ladder state via Console api/v1/degradation-ladders, (3) require opt-in for automatic small-model fallback. Action: ENG-48212 to add Console UI work.

2026-03-05: Load spike simulation: routing-policy fast-path meets p99 decision latency target (under 600us) in our dev cluster. Observed increased memory pressure due to policy cache; mitigation: bounded TTL and LRU eviction (follow-up ENG-48230).

2026-03-08: Security review kickoff. Scoped review for cross-tenant policy execution and audit logging. Initial guidance: encrypt decision logs at rest and include request fingerprint only. See https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEG-LADDER-SEC.

2026-03-10: Implemented rollout plan for internal beta: create 3 test tenants, enable shadow replay for them, and gate auto-rollback off by default. QA checklist added and owner assigned to Miguel Santos.
